title: pkix-chain: add dane Cargo feature default-on + runtime config in verify_tls_server
description:
## What

Wire DANE into pkix-chain's verify_tls_server (PKIX-fmtv.11) via the layered control model from Mark 2026-05-12.

## Cargo feature

`pkix-chain/Cargo.toml`:

```toml
[features]
default = ["dane"]
dane = ["dep:pkix-dane", "dep:pkix-dane-resolver"]
```

When `dane` is enabled (default), verify_tls_server attempts DANE. When disabled, verify_tls_server is pure-PKIX behavior.

## Runtime config

verify_tls_server gains a config struct (or builder) carrying DANE state:

- Resolver override (default: built-in pkix-dane-resolver with sensible config)
- Enable/disable toggle (runtime override of the compile-time default)
- Failure-mode policy (depends on .4)

Conceptual API:

```rust
verify_tls_server(chain, anchors, hostname, port, now, &verifier, &rev_checker)
    // -> DANE-default if compile-time enabled, runtime can override

verify_tls_server_with_config(chain, anchors, hostname, port, now, &verifier, &rev_checker, &dane_config)
    // -> explicit config for callers who care
```

OR builder pattern:

```rust
TlsServerVerifier::new(anchors)
    .with_resolver(custom_resolver)
    .with_dane_off()
    .verify(chain, hostname, port, now, ...)
```

Builder shape vs args shape is a sub-decision; file separately if needed.

## DANE flow inside verify_tls_server

1. If `dane` feature off OR runtime config dane=false: pure PKIX path (current behavior).
2. Else:
   a. Resolve TLSA records via configured resolver.
   b. If DNS/DNSSEC fails: apply failure-mode policy (.4 decision).
   c. If TLSA records absent: pure PKIX path (treat as no constraint).
   d. If TLSA records present: dispatch by usage:
      - DANE-EE (usage 3): match leaf hash; if match, return Ok bypassing chain validation.
      - DANE-TA (usage 2): synthesize TrustAnchor; add to anchor set; run verify_chain.
      - PKIX-TA (usage 0): run verify_chain; assert chain transits through TLSA-named CA.
      - PKIX-EE (usage 1): run verify_chain; assert leaf matches TLSA.
      - Multiple records: try in policy-defined order.

## Depends on

- PKIX-j32w.1 (pkix-dane)
- PKIX-j32w.2 (pkix-dane-resolver)
- PKIX-fmtv.11 (verify_tls_server foundation)
- PKIX-j32w.4 (failure-mode decision)
- PKIX-j32w.5 (DNS config source decision)

## Acceptance

- [ ] Cargo feature `dane` exists, default-on
- [ ] verify_tls_server attempts DANE when feature on and runtime config allows
- [ ] verify_tls_server is pure-PKIX when feature off
- [ ] All four DANE usages exercised in tests
- [ ] CHANGELOG entry flagging the dep tree growth
- [ ] AGENTS.md crate inventory updated to reflect pkix-chain's new shape

## Stub status

Future work. Blocks on .1 + .2 + PKIX-fmtv.11. Decision-children .4 + .5 needed before this lands.
design:
FEATURE GATE DECIDED 2026-11-24 (Mark, interactive): split the feature in two.

    [features]
    default = ["dane"]
    dane = ["dep:pkix-dane"]
    dane-resolver = ["dane", "dep:pkix-dane-resolver"]

- dane is DEFAULT-ON and pulls only pkix-dane: no_std, four small dependencies, no I/O, no network. The DANE-aware API surface (TLSA records accepted, DaneFailurePolicy honoured) is present for every consumer.
- dane-resolver is OFF by default and pulls the DNS stack (hickory, probably tokio). Turnkey DANE costs one feature flag.

## Why not both default-on, as the epic filed it

Closing PKIX-j32w.4 as opportunistic removed the fatal objection — a DNS outage now degrades to PKIX instead of breaking TLS verification. But it left a second cost standing and arguably made it worse.

With opportunistic fallback, an air-gapped or firewalled deployment does not break; it pays for a failed lookup on EVERY verification. Depending on how the network refuses, that is anywhere between an instant error and a multi-second DNS timeout. A batch audit over ten thousand certificates could add hours for a feature that cannot succeed in that environment at all. Failing closed would at least have made this loud; opportunistic makes it quiet and slow, which is harder to diagnose than an outright failure.

The second cost is dependency weight: hickory plus likely tokio in pkix-chain's default tree for every consumer, including those who never validate a TLS server certificate.

Separating 'DANE by default' from 'DNS by default' gets most of the adoption benefit at neither cost. Offline consumers are untouched and — importantly — do not need --no-default-features, so they are not forced to opt out of unrelated defaults to avoid DANE.

## What this costs the epic's premise

The epic's goal was 'zero required consumer code change'. This weakens it to 'one feature flag in Cargo.toml'. That is the honest price of keeping a network call out of everybody's default path. The compile gate, runtime setting and call-site override of the epic's three-layer control model all survive unchanged.

## Also required of this bead

- verify_tls_server gains a DANE parameter and honours DaneFailurePolicy per the spec in PKIX-j32w.4's close reason. Bogus must fail regardless of policy.
- Pure-PKIX behavior preserved when the feature is off OR when runtime config disables DANE.
- A call-site override for pure PKIX in a DANE-enabled binary (epic layer 3).
- Resolver overridable via builder / config; NoTlsaResolver is the zero-cost default already shipped in pkix-dane 0.2.0.
